objectives.text: wake someone up with “Wake up, Matt.” and ask and answer “What time is it?”
name morning routines: get up, wash his face, eat breakfast and brush her teeth
ask “What does he do in the morning?” and answer “He goes to school.”
read A Morning on a Farm, from Spain, and compare that morning with their own
read and spell words with short a, like cap, and a with a silent e, like cape
say no politely with “I'm sorry I can't. I have a piano lesson.”
name after-school activities: do homework, have a snack, watch TV and go to bed
ask “Do they do homework before dinner?” and answer “Yes, they do.” or “No, they don't.”
read Band Practice, from Canada, and talk about what they do after school
read and spell words with short i, like pin, and i with a silent e, like pine
read the time on a clock and say it, like “It's seven o'clock.”
say the numbers from 1 to 100 in English and count by tens
create a schedule of their day with a time for each activity
tell a partner about their day, like “I get up at seven o'clock.”
shop for clothes with “May I try on this jacket?” and “How do I look?”
name clothes: a dress, jeans, shorts, sneakers, a sweatshirt and a T-shirt
ask “Is she wearing sneakers?” and answer “Yes, she is.” or “No, she isn't.”
read Colorful and Stylish, from Scotland, and describe the clothes in the photos
read and spell words with short o, like hop, and o with a silent e, like hope
suggest “Let's go to the park.” and offer help with “Don't worry. I'll show you.”
name activities: in-line skating, listening to music, playing badminton and taking pictures
ask and answer “What does he like doing?” “He likes riding a bike.”
read Fun Family Activities, from Portugal, and tell what the family likes doing together
read and spell words with short u, like cub, and u with a silent e, like cube
learn the names of different exercises and how each one helps the body
explain how to do one exercise in a few short steps
create a daily exercise chart that shows what exercise they do each day
share their exercise chart and tell which exercise they like best
ask “Where are you going?” and answer “I'm going home.” or “I'm going to the playground.”
name places in town: bank, hospital, library, post office and shopping mall
ask “Are they going to the library?” and answer “Yes, they are.” or “No, they aren't.”
read The Library on the Truck, from the Netherlands, and tell why it is useful
hear and read words that start with j, like jet, and with y, like yes
order at a shop with “Can I help you?” and “Two chocolate ice cream cones, please.”
name shops: bakery, bookstore, clothing store, pet store and shoe store
tell where a shop is with behind, between or next to: “It's next to the bookstore.”
read Mr. Robot Ice Cream Shop, from Japan, and tell what is special about the shop
read and spell words that start with bl and br, like blue and brown

units.title: School Link 3 · Different places in a city

objectives.text: learn about different places in a city and what people do there
give simple directions using next to, behind and across from
draw a map of their neighborhood with labels for the main places
use their map to tell where places are, like “The bank is next to the bakery.”
ask “What day is it today?” and talk about being ready for a test
name the days of the week and school subjects like math, music, science and PE
ask “What classes does he have on Monday?” and answer “He has English and art.”
read Home Schooling, from the USA, and compare learning at home with learning at school
read and spell words that start with pl and pr, like plant and print
ask “What are you doing tomorrow?” and wish a friend “Have a great weekend.”
use always, usually, sometimes and never with activities like take a walk and walk the dog
ask “What do they do on the weekend?” and answer “They usually go shopping.”
read City Camping, from South Korea, and tell how people camp in the city
read and spell words that start with cl and cr, like clap and crab
read a pictograph chart and tell what each picture stands for
ask classmates about their favorite weekend activity and keep a tally
create a class pictograph chart of favorite weekend activities
tell what the chart shows, like “Most students like to go swimming.”
ask “What's for dinner, Mom?” and answer “We're having a barbecue.”
name rooms like the kitchen and dining room, and things like a sink, a stove and a mirror
ask “What's in the bathroom?” and answer “There's a sink and a toilet.”
read Old and New, from Germany, and compare the old and new homes in the reading
read and spell words that start with gl and gr, like glass and green
invite a friend to study with “Do you want to study together?” and “See you soon.”
name things people do at home: making dinner, feeding the dog, taking a bath and cleaning the desk
ask “Where is she?” and “What's she doing?” and answer “She's feeding the dog.”
read Time to Clean, from Mexico, and talk about how they help clean at home
read and spell words that start with fl and fr, like flag and frog

units.title: School Link 5 · Homes around the world

objectives.text: learn about different kinds of homes around the world and why people build them that way
compare a home from another country with their own home
find an interesting house on the internet and make a poster about it
present their house poster and tell where the house is and what is special about it
ask a why question and answer with because: “Because your sister needs new shoes.”
name places: airport, amusement park, beach, movie theater, museum and zoo
talk about the past with “Where were they yesterday?” “They were at the museum.”
read Safari World, from Thailand, and tell what visitors can see there
read and spell words that start with sm and sn, like smile and snow
ask “How's the weather today?” and get ready for a bike ride with “Put on your helmets.”
name weather words: sunny, cloudy, rainy, snowy, windy and foggy
ask “Was it snowy on Wednesday?” and answer “Yes, it was.” or “No, it wasn't.”
read Swimming or Skiing, from Morocco, and tell what people can do in different weather
read and spell words that start with dr and tr, like drum and tree
listen to a weather report and tell what the weather will be
give a short weather report, like “Today it's sunny and windy.”
create a weekly weather chart and fill it in each day
use their chart to tell how the weather was, like “It was rainy on Monday.”
